title: Solar position and sun light placement
purpose: Compute the sun's elevation, azimuth, declination, hour angle and equation of time for a UTC time and a latitude and longitude, with optional refraction, and turn them into a unit direction (+Y up, -Z north, +X east) that places a DirectionalLight. Use it for time-of-day lighting, shadow studies and sundial scenes.

engine.name: node
engine.notes: Pure JavaScript; aimSunLight works with any light that has position.set and an optional target, such as a three.js DirectionalLight. The demo rendered shadows with three.js 0.186.1.

contract.axes: +Y up, -Z north, +X east (three.js default camera looks north); azimuth in degrees clockwise from north

exports.name: solarPosition
exports.signature: solarPosition(date, latitude, longitude, options = {}) -> {elevation, azimuth, zenith, declination, hourAngle, equationOfTime, julianDay}
exports.summary: The sun for a UTC instant and a place; angles in degrees, equation of time in minutes; longitude east positive.

exports.name: sunDirection
exports.signature: sunDirection(date, latitude, longitude, options = {}) -> [x, y, z]
exports.summary: Unit vector toward the sun; y < 0 below the horizon.

exports.name: directionFromAngles
exports.summary: Unit vector for an azimuth (clockwise from north) and an elevation.

exports.name: julianDay
exports.summary: Julian day of a Date or epoch milliseconds.

exports.name: aimSunLight
exports.summary: Set light.position to its target plus direction * distance.

options.name: refraction
options.meaning: Add atmospheric refraction to elevation (apparent position) or leave it geometric.

limits: Low-precision solar coordinates: positions agree with published values to about 0.01 to 0.05 degrees for dates within a few centuries of 2000, not to ephemeris accuracy. Refraction uses a standard-atmosphere fit and is approximate near the horizon; time is UTC with no time zone or daylight saving handling, and longitude is east positive. It gives the sun's direction only: no sunrise and sunset search, sky colour, irradiance or moon. The scene axes are a convention (+Y up, -Z north); rotate the result for a scene with another north. Checked against published solstice, equinox and equation-of-time values and hand calculation, not against an ephemeris. Only three.js 0.186.1 shadows in headless Chrome on SwiftShader WebGL 2 were rendered.
technique_references: Low-precision solar coordinates: mean anomaly, equation of centre, apparent longitude, obliquity
Equation of time and hour angle
Spherical astronomy: altitude and azimuth from hour angle, declination and latitude
